data.name: Mechthilda
data.gender_notes: Mechthilda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Germanic elements mago (might) and hild (strife, battle). The name Mechthild means 'mighty in battle' or 'struggle'. This name is derived from the Old High German name Meginhilt, which was later Latinized as Mechthildis. The name Mechthilda carries the meaning “Struggle, strength, mighty in battle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Mechthilda usually hope their child will grow to embody struggle, strength, mighty in battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of inner strength and resilience, embodying the power to overcome challenges and adversities.
data.etymology: Mechthilda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Struggle, strength, mighty in battle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mechthilda total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: מֵכְתִילְדָה
in_hebrew.meaning: מלכה - meaning queen, ruler, and mighty one.
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם - Mechthilda - נגזר מהשם הבריטוני - Maenwenna, המורכב מMaen - עז, חזק, ו-wenna - queen, ruler. בערבית - Malkah - מלכה, ראש, וביוונית - basilissa - מלכה, ראש. לפי ההיסטוריה - Mechthilda הייתה נזירה ירושלמית, והשם נקשר לעוצמה, חזקות, ועדינות. באגדה - Mechthilda הייתה קדושה, חזקה, וראש המאורע. מקורה של Mechthilda - בערבית - Malkah, והוא מסמל - ראש, עוצמה, וגודל. על-פי ההיסטוריה - Mechthilda - היה נזיר, ואחד מ-12 נזירי ירושלים.

in_greek.name: Μέχθιλδα
in_greek.meaning: Βασίλισσα - meaning queen, ruler, strong one.
in_greek.long_meaning: Πηγή του ονόματος - Μέχθιλδα - προέρχεται από το βρετανικό όνομα - Μαινουέννα, που αποτελείται από τα μέρη - Μαιν - ισχυρός, δυνατός και Βεννά - βασίλισσα, κυρία. Στην αραβική - Μαλκά - βασίλισσα, αρχή και στην ελληνική - βασιλίσσα - βασίλισσα, αρχή. Σύμφωνα με την ιστορία - Μέχθιλδα ήταν μοναχή της Ιερουσαλήμ και το όνομα συνδέεται με τη δύναμη, την ενέργεια και την ευγένεια. Στην αφήγηση - Μέχθιλδα ήταν άγιος, δυνατός και αρχηγός των γεγονότων. Πηγή του ονόματος - Μαλκά, που αντιπροσωπεύει την αρχή, τη δύναμη και την μεγαλοπρέπεια. Σύμφωνα με την ιστορία - Μέχθιλδα ήταν μοναχή και ένα από τα 12 μοναχούς της Ιερουσαλήμ.

in_latin.name: Mechthilda
in_latin.meaning: Rex - meaning strong, mighty, and powerful one.
in_latin.long_meaning: Origo nominis - Mechthilda - derivata est a nomine Britannico - Maenwenna, quod constat ex partibus - Maen - potens, fortis et Wenna - regina, domina. In Arabic - Malca - regina, principis et in Graeco - basilissa - regina, principis. Secundum historiam - Mechthilda erat monacha Hierosolymitana et nomen connectio est cum potestate, energia, et gentilitate. In narratione - Mechthilda erat sanctus, potens, et princeps eventorum. Origo nominis - Malca, quae representat principem, potestatem, et magnificenciam. Secundum historiam - Mechthilda erat monacha et unus ex duodecim monachis Hierosolymitanis.

in_english.name: Mechthilda
in_english.meaning: Strong, mighty, powerful, and queenly one with gentle and meek spirit.
in_english.long_meaning: Origin of the name - Mechthilda - is derived from the British name - Maenwenna, which consists of the parts - Maen - strong, mighty, and Wenna - queen, ruler. According to history - Mechthilda was a Jerusalemite nun, and the name is connected with power, energy, and gentleness. In legend - Mechthilda was a saint, strong, and the leader of the events. Origin of the name - Malca, which represents the leader, power, and magnificence. According to history - Mechthilda was a nun and one of the 12 nuns of Jerusalem. The name Mechthilda is also associated with the qualities of a queen, a leader, and a strong woman. In modern times, the name Mechthilda is given to girls who are expected to grow up to be strong, confident, and independent women. The name Mechthilda has been used in various forms and spellings throughout history, including Mechtilde, Mechthild, and Mechthildis. The name Mechthilda is also associated with the qualities of a saint, a martyr, and a devoted servant of God.

data.cultural_impact: Mechthild was a popular name among European royalty and noble families during the Middle Ages. The name is associated with strong women who were known for their courage and determination. Mechthild of Bavaria, for instance, was a 13th-century Benedictine abbess who was known for her spiritual wisdom and her efforts to improve the lives of her nuns. Her hagiography, "The Flowering Rod," is a classic in German literature. Another Mechthild, this time a duchess of Franconia, was a patron of the arts and supported the foundations of several important institutions, including the University of Erfurt and the Calvary Chapel at Rothenburg. The name Mechthild continues to be used in various German-speaking countries and has a rich cultural history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mechthild has spiritual significance as a reminder of the strength and courage that each person possesses within themselves. It encourages us to face our struggles and battles with determination and faith. Mechthild is also a name that evokes the image of a warrior-saint, a woman who was dedicated to serving God and living a spiritual life despite the challenges and hardships she faced. The name inspires us to be like Mechthild, to be mighty in our spiritual battles and to never give up in our pursuit of God. By bearing this name, we are reminded of the power that lies within us and called to live up to the name's rich spiritual heritage.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mechthilda, derived from the Germanic name "Mechtildis," means "strong in battle, mighty in God." This name symbolizes a woman of great strength and devotion, shining the light of faith in the midst of life's challenges.

historical_references.reference: Mechthild of Magdeburg, a German mystic and poetess, was born around 1210 or 1220 and died between 1282 and 1294. She is best known for her mystical work, the 'Flowers of Holy Living', which she wrote in the mid-13th century.

Mechthild of Alsace, also known as Mechthild of the White Hands, was a Benedictine nun and a German mystic. She was born in the early 13th century and died around 1295. Her work, 'The Flowing Light of the Godhead', is considered one of the most influential mystical texts of the Middle Ages.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mechthildis, also known as Mechthild or Mechtilde, is a medieval German saint and mystic. Her life story has been a source of inspiration for various artistic works in modern times. In Gothic literature, her experiences of mystical visions and ecstasies have been explored in novels such as Anathema by Rita Angelina. Historical fiction authors like Roger Sherman Hoar have retold her story in a more narrative format. In gaming, Mechthild is featured as a character in the role-playing game, Dragon Age: Inquisition, and in the strategy game, Hex: Shards of Fate. Her story continues to resonate with modern audiences, particularly those interested in spirituality and the supernatural.
